articles.title: AI cloud firm CoreWeave enters India, plans 240 MW data centre in Navi Mumbai with AdaniConneX
articles.description: US-based AI cloud computing company CoreWeave recently announced its entry into India through a collaboration with AdaniConneX, with plans to deploy 240 megawatts (MW) of data centre capacity in Navi Mumbai. The Nasdaq-listed company said the expansion will bring its AI cloud platform closer to Indian customers, providing enterprises with specialised computing infrastructure, software and services to develop, deploy and scale AI applications. The planned development will comprise three buildings, each with 80 MW of capacity, at AdaniConneX's Taloja campus in Navi Mumbai. CoreWeave will be the sole tenant across all three buildings, with an opportunity to add a further 240 MW at the site, potentially taking its total capacity there to 480 MW. The first phase is expected to become available in mid-2028, with additional capacity scheduled to come online in stages. The company has not disclosed the financial value of the proposed investment. CoreWeave to deploy NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform As part of the project, CoreWeave plans to deploy NVIDIA's Vera Rubin platform on its AI cloud infrastructure in India to support workloads including AI model training, inference, reasoning and agentic AI applications. The Taloja facilities are being designed for high-density AI computing, with direct liquid cooling for graphics processing unit (GPU) data halls and a non-evaporative chilled water system. According to CoreWeave, the infrastructure is intended to accommodate future generations of AI computing technology as processing requirements evolve. The company also plans to establish an office in India and hire local employees to work with customers and partners. However, it has not specified the location of the proposed office, the number of employees it intends to recruit or a timeline for establishing its local operations. “India has the talent, developers, and ambition to become a major center of AI innovation,” said Sachin Jain, COO of CoreWeave. “We are investing in the infrastructure, technology, and local presence needed to support that growth, bringing 240 megawatts of capacity, NVIDIA Vera Rubin, and CoreWeave’s expertise to customers building and scaling AI in India,” he said. Expansion aligns with India's AI infrastructure ambitions CoreWeave said its planned investment supports India's efforts to expand domestic AI capabilities, including the government's IndiaAI Mission. The mission, approved by the Union Cabinet in March 2024, aims to strengthen the country's AI ecosystem through improved access to computing infrastructure, support for innovation and the development of AI applications. The company's entry into India comes as demand grows for specialised infrastructure capable of handling increasingly complex AI workloads. CoreWeave said the expansion reflects rising customer demand for its AI cloud services and its strategy of bringing computing capacity closer to enterprises and developers across international markets. Its Indian partner, AdaniConneX, is a 50:50 joint venture between Adani Enterprises and US-based data centre operator EdgeConneX. In February 2026, Adani Group announced plans to expand its data centre infrastructure towards a 5 GW target, building on what it described as AdaniConneX's existing 2 GW national data centre platform. The plans form part of the group's broader strategy to develop AI-ready infrastructure in India. CoreWeave expands global AI cloud footprint The India announcement follows CoreWeave's expansion into Indonesia in August 2026, when it announced three data centre facilities with a combined 360 MW of contracted IT power, expected to become operational in 2028. The developments extend the company's international presence beyond its established operations in North America and Europe. As of 11 August 2026, CoreWeave had approximately 4.2 gigawatts of contracted power globally, up from about 3.7 gigawatts at the end of June, according to a company announcement in September. Contracted power represents capacity secured for the company's infrastructure plans and does not necessarily mean that all of it is operational. Founded in 2017, CoreWeave provides cloud computing infrastructure designed for AI workloads, serving AI developers, startups, research laboratories and large enterprises. The company became publicly traded on the Nasdaq stock exchange in March 2025 under the ticker symbol CRWV. Its planned Navi Mumbai development will mark another expansion of its international AI infrastructure network, although the first phase is not expected to become available until mid-2028.
